issue_context.title: Add a metric to track reasons for unschedulable pods
issue_context.body:
#### What would you like to be added:

A metric that tracks reasons for currently unschedulable pods in a cluster. Breaking down the metric by pod name is not scalable because of cardinality, but we can break down by plugin name.

_Suggested Semantics_
```
unschedulableReasons = metrics.NewGaugeVec(		
    &metrics.GaugeOpts{
			Subsystem:      SchedulerSubsystem,
			Name:           "unschedulable_pods_by_plugin",
			Help:           "The number of unschedulable pods broken down by plugin name. A pod will increment the gauge for all plugins that caused it to not schedule and so this metric have meaning only when broken down by plugin.",
			StabilityLevel: metrics.ALPHA,
		}, []string{"plugin", "profile"})
```

Each unschedulable pod increases the gauge for all plugins that caused the pod to fail (since each pod is assessed against multiple nodes and so a pod may have one or more reasons for not being schedulable). One issue here is the gauge will have clear meaning only when broken down by plugin (number of pods unschedulable because of that plugin), but the aggregate will not have a meaning.

**_**Possible implementation:**_**
We track the plugins that caused a pod to not schedule in [QueuedPodInfo](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/b766721332da82f8a3eaa7dd3f131713d291f288/pkg/scheduler/framework/types.go#L106), every time we add/remove an unschedulable pod we update the gauge.

#### Why is this needed:

This is important to setup alerts on specific reasons that may cause pods to not schedule in a cluster.

/sig scheduling
comments:
/triage accepted
/assign

> /triage accepted
> /assign

We still need to discuss the issue.

> > /triage accepted
> > /assign
> 
> We still need to discuss the issue.

Sure
@logicalhan what do you think about the proposal? Especially the part where the guage metric has no value as aggregate, but only when broken down by its labels?

I think that pattern is okay, many metrics are already like that. For instance, the aggregate request counts/latencies for WATCH and POSTS isn't particularly meaningful, they are meaningful only within their respective drilldowns.

Sounds good, I think we can move forward then.

@yuzhiquan are you still interested in doing this? do you have any questions on how to do it?

> The number of unschedulable pods broken down by plugin name. A pod will increment the gauge for all plugins that caused it to not schedule and so this metric have meaning only when broken down by plugin.

How come this is not a counter metric? That's what I'd expect to see.

Because we need to track the current number of unschedulable pods, which goes up and down like a gauge. 

A counter may work (take the delta) if we are able to increment it once per unique pod, but I don't believe we can reliably do that.

Sometimes you can do this with two counters - incrementing one when a Pod becomes unschedulable and the other (using the same label for relevant plugin) when that particular plugin ceases to contribute to any Pod being unschedulable.

Thinking this through but not in depth, I believe that you don't have to track the names of Pods to use this technique. 

By themselves these counters aren't so useful, but the diff between them can be.
@ahg-g I can pick this up if its not assigned yet

Yes please go ahead.

/assign @hprateek43

> Sometimes you can do this with two counters - incrementing one when a Pod becomes unschedulable and the other (using the same label for relevant plugin) when that particular plugin ceases to contribute to any Pod being unschedulable.
> 
> Thinking this through but not in depth, I believe that you don't have to track the names of Pods to use this technique.
> 
> By themselves these counters aren't so useful, but the diff between them can be.

What you're describing is a gauge.

I've heard it said that a gauge is appropriate if-and-only-if a `SUM` operation on the measurements does not make sense for any time interval. I think people might well care about aggregates on these metrics.

It is still not clear to me how we can efficiently implement what you are proposing. 

> Thinking this through but not in depth, I believe that you don't have to track the names of Pods to use this technique.

I would like to understand more details about how we can avoid this, otherwise I think we should go with a gauge.
@alculquicondor I'm not picturing why 2 counters is more of a problem than 1 counter. I'd be happy to explain my thoughts on metric design more - is there a Google Doc for this or anything?

The comparison would be against 1 gauge. After a restart, there are no "unschedulable" pods, so we can reset it to zero.

All the discussion is happening in this thread for now.
Counters are allowed to reset to 0, so there's no need to write special code to handle component failure. https://www.robustperception.io/how-does-a-prometheus-counter-work/ has more on this.

We already have a counter metric that tracks scheduling attempts broken down by result. 

@sftim to achieve the semantics described in the issue using two counters, I believe we need to count unique pods not attempts, this is not currently available in the scheduler.

> Each unschedulable pod increases the gauge for all plugins that caused the pod to fail (since each pod is assessed against multiple nodes and so a pod may have one or more reasons for not being schedulable)

OK, so this incrementation part is the easy part, and the hard bit would be to work out how to decrement the gauge? Have I got that right?

If we would confidently know when to decrement that gauge, perhaps could we instead increment the second (successes) counter. The way I picture it, those two things (decrement gauge | increment second counter) should happen under exactly identical conditions.

I think it would be OK to have a gauge metric as well. However, if this can end up being an aggregable counter, I think that's even better.

> While I can see the benefit of @sftim's proposal, I think that 2 counters would be problematic when there's a scheduler restart.
> 
> @logicalhan any thoughts?

It would be the same..
I would go with the gauge then.
